source.title: Tree Spanners on Chordal Graphs: Complexity, Algorithms, Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Given a connected graph G, a spanning tree T is a tree 3-spanner when every pair of vertices x and y has tree distance d_T(x, y) at most 3 times graph distance d_G(x, y). A graph is chordal when it has no chordless cycle of length at least four, and a graph is strongly chordal when it is chordal and has no induced k-sun for any k >= 3. Is there an efficient algorithm to decide whether a chordal graph, and in particular whether a strongly chordal graph, admits a tree 3-spanner?

For a chordal graph G, let r(G) be the radius of G and diam(G) be the diameter of G. Is there an efficient algorithm to decide, for chordal graphs satisfying diam(G) = 2r(G) - 2, whether G admits a tree (2r(G) - 1)-spanner, meaning a spanning tree T in which d_T(x, y) <= (2r(G) - 1)d_G(x, y) for every pair of vertices x and y?

evidence.quote: be decided efficiently on chordal graphs

accepted.question_text: For an integer t >= 3, what is the computational complexity of deciding whether a chordal graph G with diameter at most t admits a tree t-spanner, that is, a spanning tree preserving all graph distances up to multiplicative stretch t?
accepted.context_brief: Chordal graphs of diameter at most t

evidence.quote: What is the complexity of Tree t-Spanner

accepted.question_text: A path graph is an intersection graph of paths in a tree. For fixed t >= 3, what is the complexity of deciding whether a path graph admits a tree t-spanner? In particular, what is the status for t = 3 on path graphs that are also strongly chordal?
